evidence.note: Created a structured task list decomposing subsystems and set statuses; gives a done-vs-pending picture, but completion is judged by code written, not test evidence.
Marked multiple subsystem tasks 'completed' — coarse progress tracking, but never tied to actual pass counts since tests had not run successfully.
Attempted to run the full test suite only twice; no visible pass/fail baseline or pass-rate-by-area reconciliation was ever established.

~160 steps spent looping on a single offline npm-install blocker (cache keys, accept headers, tar tarballs). Diagnosed variedly but never stepped back or returned to quantifying test progress — the opposite of recognizing and breaking a loop.

reasoning: The agent maintained a task list tracking which subsystems it had built vs. pending, placing it above the vague-recollection level (3). But it never obtained a real pass count, marked subsystems done from code-completion rather than test evidence, and never reconciled done-vs-remaining against the suite — so it falls short of the anchor-5 requirement to track pass counts and re-check for regressions. The extended, unbroken install loop across the whole back half further argues against the higher anchors, which require recognizing when one is looping and stepping back. This lands at 4.
